newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WORKERS TO VOTE ON DUFERCO BUY OF CLABECQ.
newsitem.headline: WORKERS TO VOTE ON DUFERCO BUY OF CLABECQ.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt Belgian steel firm Forges de Clabecq will be asked to give their view on the planned partial takeover by Italian-Swiss group Duferco in a referendum this week, union sources said on Monday.
The referendum is aimed at breaking the deadlock over the deal created by local union leader Roberto D'Orazio who has said he wants more jobs guarantees before backing the takeover.
Duferco had threatened to drop its bid after D'Orazio said late last week a referendum could not be held because too many of Clabecq's 1,800 workers were on holiday.
After mediation at the Labour Ministry national union leaders overruled D'Orazio on Monday and said Clabecq workers would be invited to vote by mail. Results are to be known by Friday, July 18.
D'Orazio, who has led the fight for jobs since the steel firm was declared bankrupt in January, called for boycott.

He has said unresolved issues included back pay due to workers from the Walloon regional government, a redundancy programme for those workers not re-employed by Duferco and early retirement provisions.
Duferco, which agreed with the Walloon region, Clabecq's largest shareholder earlier this month on a partial purchase of the company, aims to take over only about 900 jobs.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy after the European Commission banned the southern region of Wallonia from injecting 1.5 billion francs ($41 million) into the loss-making firm and ordered the company to reimburse subsidies already granted.
Clabecq has appealed the Commission's decision before the European Court of First Instance.
